newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Krasnoyarsk aluminium plant gets new CEO.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Krasnoyarsk aluminium plant gets new CEO.

text.p: Russia's Krasnoyarsk aluminium smelter has appointed a new chief executive officer, a company spokesman said on Monday.
Georgy Pashkov, the plant's Moscow-based representative, said the smelter's board had elected Igor Vishnyovsky as general director after the previous head, Yuri Kolpakov, resigned.
Kolpakov, under investigation by the Interior Ministry for alleged financial misdealings, had been appointed first deputy general director in charge of development, Pashkov said.
Vishnyovsky is also president of Krazpa-Metals, a 50-50 joint venture between Krasnoyarsk and Swiss-based commodities trader Glencore AG of Switzerland.
Krasnoyarsk, which is Russia's and the world's second largest aluminium smelter, accounted for 27 percent of Russia's total primary aluminium output last year of 2.87 million tonnes.
Pashkov said earlier this month that Kolpakov had evidence to clear his name.
